safetyNote: Listed as edible by DGfM and Swiss VAPKO, but identification must be secure and the mushroom properly cooked. Check a fresh cut: its scant latex is wine-red immediately, whereas the similar L. semisanguifluus first releases orange latex that reddens later. Confirm the pine habitat and other characters; do not identify from colour or a drawing alone. DGfM marks this species Red List category 2 in Germany, so respect local conservation and collecting rules.

sections.title: Subtle orange and wine tones
sections.text: The cap reaches about 12 cm across, initially convex with a long-inrolled margin and then broadly depressed. It is dull ochre-orange to grey-orange with reddish-wine tones, usually weakly zoned or unzoned. The surface is slightly tacky when wet and may acquire small greenish patches with age or handling, but generally greens less strongly than L. semisanguifluus.

sections.title: Pink gills and red milk from the start
sections.text: Crowded, narrow gills are attached to shortly decurrent, pale cream-pink at first and increasingly pink or wine-red. The short, pale pinkish to wine-tinted stem may have scattered shallow reddish pits and becomes cavernous or hollow with age. Firm flesh is pale in the centre and wine-red near its outer layers. A fresh cut produces rather scant, thick wine-red latex immediately: this timing is the key field character, not merely a red stain seen later.

sections.title: Pine woods and comparisons
sections.text: This European milkcap grows with pines, notably in calcareous Mediterranean woodland, and fruits chiefly from summer into autumn according to locality. L. semisanguifluus initially exudes orange milk that changes to wine-red over several minutes and commonly develops stronger green staining. L. deliciosus also begins with orange milk, while the fir-associated L. salmonicolor has a bright salmon cap. Host tree, latex at the instant of injury, gill colour and cap zones should be assessed together.

sections.title: Edibility and conservation
sections.text: University of Lyon 1 rates L. sanguifluus an excellent edible species; DGfM and VAPKO include it in their edible mushroom lists. DGfM marks it Red List category 2 in Germany, a regional conservation status that should discourage indiscriminate collecting there. Gather only confidently identified specimens in good condition and cook them adequately. This illustration cannot show the timing of the latex reaction or establish the host tree.

traits: Dull ochre-orange to grey-orange cap with wine tones, generally weakly zoned, to about 12 cm
Crowded pale pink to wine-red gills, attached to shortly decurrent
Short pale pinkish stem, sometimes with scattered reddish pits, hollowing with age
Scant wine-red latex immediately on cutting; pale central flesh and wine-red outer flesh
Pine associate, often on calcareous Mediterranean soil; summer to autumn
Less extensive green staining than many related orange milkcaps
